learning_outcomes.text: Students learn the operational functional areas in an overview and selected concepts of corporate management/strategy development.
Students know and understand the principles and methods of systematic decision-making.
Students know the purposes of cost and activity accounting (KLR) and the structure of a KLR system.
They are familiar with important instruments of KLR, cost center and cost unit accounting, and short-term income statements.
They are able to perform and evaluate cost center and order-related actual-to-target comparisons (SIV).
They can apply partial cost accounting in the form of contribution margin accounting.
They are able to perform decision calculations based on KLR.
Students know various digital media for learning organization and can apply them.
Students are able to purposefully select both analog and digital teaching and learning content for their studies.
Students are able to handle digital media competently and purposefully.
Students can organize their studies in terms of time and content and process the abundance of information purposefully.
Students are enabled to work in KLR in a transparent, structured, and decision-oriented manner.
Students become aware that KLR must be designed for a specific purpose.
Students are enabled to work independently.
Students acquire competencies in dealing with digital media.
Students learn strategies for acquiring knowledge using blended learning methods.
Students learn independent and problem-, solution-, or action-oriented work through exercises.
Students practice partner and teamwork in the exercises.

syllabus_topics: Purposes of KLR and cost allocation principles
Specific cost accounting content in the areas of AI and CS
KLR on a full cost basis
KLR on a partial cost basis (contribution margin accounting)
Decision-oriented KLR including the principle of relevant costs
Digital media in the student learning context
Digital media in science and communication
Media usage and pillars of media literacy
teaching_methods: Seminar-style instruction with group and partner work
